tools.name: prepare_machine
tools.description:
Runs "kasy doctor" to check whether this computer is ready to build Kasy apps (Flutter SDK, Dart, Ruby/CocoaPods on macOS, and backend CLIs). Call this when the user asks to set up, prepare, or check their machine for Kasy.

This is step 1 of a loop, not a one-shot report. You are running on the user's own machine with real execution access via run_setup_command. Use it:

1. Call this tool and read the report line by line.
2. Fix ONLY what the user's intended backend needs. Do not install Firebase tooling "just in case":
   - Always: Flutter, Dart, Node, FVM (and CocoaPods/Xcode tooling on macOS when relevant). FVM is best-effort: `kasy new` pins a per-project Flutter version with it when available and silently falls back to the global Flutter SDK when it's not, so don't treat a missing FVM as a blocker.
   - Backend Firebase (or prepare "all" / push planned): Firebase CLI, FlutterFire, gcloud, and aligned Google logins.
   - Backend Supabase without push: Supabase CLI + supabase login only. Do NOT install firebase-tools, flutterfire_cli, or gcloud, and do NOT demand Firebase login.
   - Backend API without push: base env only. Same: no Firebase/gcloud unless they will enable push.
   - Push later on Supabase/API: Firebase tools are installed when they run kasy add notifications / add_feature notifications, not during prepare.
3. For every item that is actually missing for that scope: decide the right install/fix command for this OS yourself (Homebrew on macOS, choco/winget on Windows, apt/dnf on Linux, or the tool's own installer, e.g. "npm install -g supabase", and only when Firebase is in scope "dart pub global activate flutterfire_cli" / "npm install -g firebase-tools"), then call run_setup_command to actually run it.
4. Call check_kasy_updates. If an update is available, explain briefly and call upgrade_kasy (or ask for an MCP client restart when check says so). Do not call create_project until check_kasy_updates passes after restart.
5. Read the "Google Cloud + Firebase login" section ONLY when a Firebase project will be created (backend firebase, OR Supabase/API with push=true). If gcloud and Firebase are on different Google accounts in that case, stop and have the user align them before create_project: "firebase login --reauth" with the same email as "gcloud auth login". Quick Supabase/API WITHOUT push does NOT need Firebase/gcloud alignment.
6. Call prepare_machine again to confirm. Repeat until everything required for the chosen backend passes, or until you hit something only the user can do (click a permission dialog, complete a login/auth flow, provide a value only they know). That is the one legitimate reason to stop.
7. DO NOT stop after just diagnosing and describing what's missing. Reporting a problem without attempting to fix it is not an acceptable outcome here. You have the means to fix it; use them.
8. Whether you fully fixed it, partially fixed it, or got stuck, call report_issue at the end: what OS this was, what was broken, and exactly what you did about it (the command that worked, or what you tried if it's still broken). This is what lets the Kasy team close real gaps in "kasy doctor" itself.
9. Never fabricate a "ready" status. Only report success when the actual tool output says so. A machine can be ready for Supabase without Firebase CLI installed.

tools.name: run_setup_command
tools.description:
Executes ONE shell command on this machine. This is the actual "fix it" step for prepare_machine (and for anything else that needs a local install/config change) — the tool only runs what YOU decide is right for this OS, it does not have its own list of fixes. Use the standard package manager for the detected OS: Homebrew on macOS, choco/winget on Windows, apt/dnf on Linux, or the tool's own installer (dart pub global activate, npm install -g, ...).

Rules:
1. One command per call. Chain with && only when the steps are genuinely one unit (e.g. "brew tap x/y && brew install z").
2. Never use sudo or anything that needs an interactive password/admin prompt — it will hang. If a fix genuinely requires elevation, tell the user the exact command and ask them to run it themselves; do not attempt it here.
3. Never destructive (no rm -rf, format, disk operations, shutdown/reboot). Installs and config only.
4. After running, call prepare_machine again to confirm the fix actually worked — do not assume success from exit code alone.
5. Once confirmed, call report_issue with resolved=true, the OS, and exactly which command fixed it. If you try reasonable fixes and it's still broken, call report_issue with resolved=false and what you tried — but only after actually trying, not as a first resort.

command.description: The exact shell command to run, e.g. "brew install cocoapods".

reason.description: One sentence: what this fixes and why.

tools.name: check_kasy_updates
tools.description:
Checks whether the running kasy-mcp session and its bundled kasy-cli are behind npm latest.

Call this before create_project (and after prepare_machine when the user will scaffold a new app). If an update is available:
1. Tell the user briefly in chat (version numbers).
2. If recommendedAction is "upgrade_kasy", call upgrade_kasy (not run_kasy_command — kasy upgrade is blocked inside MCP).
3. If recommendedAction is "restart_mcp_client" (common with npx -y kasy-mcp), ask the user to fully quit and reopen the app where the assistant runs — any IDE or AI client with MCP (do not name a specific product unless the user mentioned theirs).
4. Do NOT call create_project in the same session after upgrading until the user has restarted the MCP client and you have confirmed with check_kasy_updates again.

Never tell users to run kasy upgrade from inside MCP — use upgrade_kasy instead. They may still run kasy upgrade in a separate terminal for a global CLI they use outside MCP.

tools.name: upgrade_kasy
tools.description:
Runs "npm install -g kasy-cli@latest kasy-mcp@latest" — the same packages kasy upgrade updates in a terminal.

Use when check_kasy_updates reports recommendedAction "upgrade_kasy". Do NOT use run_kasy_command for upgrade (blocked inside MCP).

If check_kasy_updates says restart_mcp_client only (typical for npx installs with no global kasy-mcp), skip this tool and ask for a client restart instead.

After a successful install, ask the user to fully quit and reopen the app where the assistant runs (IDE or AI client with MCP). That reloads the MCP server with the new version. Do NOT call create_project in this same chat session — wait until they are back after restart, run check_kasy_updates again, then create_project.

tools.name: create_project_status
tools.description:
Checks whether a background create_project is still running, finished successfully, or failed.

Use this after create_project returns status "running", or when the MCP client timed out (-32001) but you are not sure whether kasy new finished.

- running: kasy new still going (see logTail)
- ready: kit_setup.json exists at projectPath
- failed: process exited without a valid project
- none: no session and no kit_setup.json at the path

parentDirectory.description: Parent folder where the project is being created. Same value as create_project.

projectPath.description: Absolute or relative path to the project folder. Overrides directory + parentDirectory.

Actions:
- list: see every column and every task (with id, title, description, columnId, order, priority, timestamps). Always start here — you need real column/task ids before you can move, update, or delete anything. This is also how you answer things like "what's left to do" or "what can we work on today": look at the columns that aren't the last one (usually "Done"/"Concluído") and read their tasks.
- create_column: name required. order optional (appends at the end if omitted).
- update_column: id + name required (rename only — there's no separate reorder-single-column op, use reorder_columns for that).
- delete_column: id required. Deletes every task inside it too (cascades on both backends) — confirm with structured quiz before calling if the column isn't empty.
- reorder_columns: ids required, an array of every column id in the new left-to-right order (not just the one that moved).
- create_task: title + columnId required. description and priority ("low"|"medium"|"high"|"urgent") optional. order optional (appends at the end of that column if omitted).
- update_task: id required, plus at least one of title/description/priority. To clear the priority, pass priority: "none". This does NOT move the task between columns — use move_task for that.
- move_task: id + columnId required (the destination column, even if unchanged). order optional (appends at the end of the destination column if omitted) — this is "move this card to column X".
- delete_task: id required.
- reorder_tasks: ids required, an array of every task id in the new order. Only reorder within one column at a time (mixing columns will desync each task's own columnId).
